definitions.explanation: The main subject or central idea of a work, discussion, or research. More formal and literary than テーマ.

examples.japanese: {論文|ろんぶん}の{主題|しゅだい}を{決|き}めた。
examples.english: I decided on the topic of my thesis.

examples.japanese: この{映画|えいが}の{主題|しゅだい}は{家族|かぞく}の{絆|きずな}だ。
examples.english: The theme of this movie is family bonds.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}の{主題|しゅだい}から{外|はず}れないように{発言|はつげん}してください。
examples.english: Please keep your remarks on the subject of the meeting.

notes:
{主題|しゅだい} refers to the central subject or theme of a work, discussion, or research. It is more formal and literary than テーマ.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {主題|しゅだい}{歌|か}: theme song
- {主題|しゅだい}{曲|きょく}: theme music
- {主題|しゅだい}を{決|き}める: to decide on a theme
- {主題|しゅだい}から{外|はず}れる: to stray from the topic

SIMILAR WORDS:
- テーマ: theme (loanword, used in everyday conversation)
- {題名|だいめい}: title (of a book, movie, etc.)
- {話題|わだい}: topic of conversation (more casual)
- {議題|ぎだい}: agenda item (for meetings)

USAGE:
In everyday speech, テーマ is far more common. {主題|しゅだい} appears in academic writing, literary criticism, and formal discussions. The compound {主題|しゅだい}{歌|か}/{主題|しゅだい}{曲|きょく} (theme song/music) is the most familiar use for most speakers.
